refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a JSON object variant from an array of key/value pairs

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: sd_json_variant_new_object() allocates a new JSON object variant and returns it in ret. The object's fields are taken from array, which must contain n variants, alternating between keys and values: the elements at even indexes are the keys and must be JSON string variants, each followed by the variant to use as the value for that key. n hence must be even. The order of the fields is retained. The referenced variants are not consumed, the new object takes its own references to them (or copies them). If n is zero, array may be NULL and an empty object is returned.

Each key may only be used once within the same object. If two or more keys in array are equal (compared byte-wise, i.e. case-sensitively, after any escaping has been resolved), the call fails with -ENOTUNIQ. JSON (as defined by RFC 8259) recommends, but does not require, keys to be unique, and implementations differ in how they treat duplicates. Since every JSON object in this library is ultimately created through this function — this includes objects generated by the parser (see sd_json_parse3) and the builder (see sd_json_build3) — no sd_json_variant object can ever contain duplicate keys. Lookups by key (e.g. via sd_json_variant_by_key()) hence are always unambiguous.

Use sd_json_variant_set_field() or sd_json_variant_merge_object() to derive a new object from an existing one with fields added or replaced; these calls drop any previous field of the same name before adding the new one, and hence do not fail on duplicate keys.

refsect1.title: Return Value
refsect1.para: On success, sd_json_variant_new_object() returns 0. On failure, it returns a negative errno-style error code. On failure ret is not modified.

refsect2.title: Errors
refsect2.para: Returned errors may indicate the following problems:

listitem.para: An argument is invalid, n is not even, or one of the elements at an even index of array is not a JSON string.
The same key is specified more than once in array.
The resulting object would be nested too deeply.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: Before version 263 objects with duplicate keys were accepted by sd_json_variant_new_object().
